recall: Hot deserts have very dry air, clear skies and a large daily temperature range.

Today we begin a new module: weather and climate.

situation: Nafissatou flies from Garoua to Douala. The pilot announces: "We are flying at 11,000 metres. The temperature outside is minus 50 degrees Celsius."
Nafissatou is surprised, because in Garoua it is 35°C and the plane is closer to the sun. She does not understand why the air is so cold up there.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Nafissatou does not understand why the air is very cold high above the ground, although it is closer to the sun.
What is the temperature outside the plane, and at what height?
The temperature is minus 50°C at a height of 11,000 metres.
What can passengers do to be comfortable during such a flight?
The plane is pressurised and heated, and passengers can carry a light jacket.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the air around the Earth, its layers, and the ozone layer that protects us from the sun.

qa.q: The Earth is surrounded by a layer of gases held by gravity. What is it called?
qa.a: This layer of gases is called the atmosphere.

qa.q: Which two gases make up most of the atmosphere?
qa.a: Nitrogen makes up about 78% and oxygen about 21% of the atmosphere. Argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour make up the rest.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: The atmosphere is the layer of gases that surrounds the Earth and is held by gravity. It is made of about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 1% other gases.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Name the four main layers of the atmosphere from the ground upwards.
qa.a: From the ground upwards, the layers are the troposphere, the stratosphere, the mesosphere and the thermosphere.

sum.title: II. Structure
items: From the ground upwards, the atmosphere has four main layers: the troposphere, the stratosphere, the mesosphere and the thermosphere.

qa.title: Question 1
qa.q: Look at the graph. What happens to temperature as we go up in the troposphere? Why was it −50°C outside the plane?
qa.a: In the troposphere, temperature falls by about 6.5°C for every 1,000 metres. At 11,000 metres, it is about 70°C colder than on the ground.

qa.q: Where do clouds, rain and wind form?
qa.a: Clouds, rain and wind form in the troposphere. It contains most of the water vapour of the atmosphere.

qa.title: Question 3
qa.q: What happens to temperature in the stratosphere? Why?
qa.a: In the stratosphere, temperature rises with height, because the ozone layer absorbs the ultraviolet rays of the sun.

sum.title: III. Thermal Structure
sum.intro: The thermal structure is the way temperature changes with height in each layer:
items: It goes from the ground to about 12 km (up to 16 km above the Equator). Temperature falls by about 6.5°C per 1,000 m. All weather takes place here.
It goes from about 12 km to 50 km. Temperature rises with height, because the ozone layer absorbs the ultraviolet rays of the sun.

qa.q: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere. What is its role?
qa.a: The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays of the sun and protects living things.

qa.q: In the 1980s, scientists found a "hole" in the ozone layer over Antarctica. What caused it?
qa.a: It was caused by chemicals called CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons), used in old refrigerators, air conditioners and spray cans.

qa.q: What are the effects of a thinner ozone layer, and what has been done?
qa.a: More UV rays cause skin cancer, eye diseases and damage to crops. The Montreal Protocol (1987) banned CFCs, and the ozone layer is slowly recovering.

sum.title: IV. Ozone Layer Depletion
defs: The ozone layer is a layer of ozone gas in the stratosphere, about 15 to 35 km high, that absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun.
Ozone layer depletion is the thinning of the ozone layer.
items: Depletion is caused by chemicals such as CFCs, used in old refrigerators, air conditioners and spray cans.
More ultraviolet rays reach the Earth, causing skin cancer, eye diseases (cataracts) and damage to crops.
The Montreal Protocol (1987), signed by Cameroon, banned CFCs. People should use ozone-friendly refrigerators and sprays.

evaluation: Why is the troposphere important for weather?
It is important because it contains most of the water vapour, so clouds, rain and wind form there.
Explain why temperature rises with height in the stratosphere.
It rises because the ozone layer absorbs the ultraviolet rays of the sun and warms the air.
Give one cause and one effect of ozone layer depletion.
One cause is the use of CFCs. One effect is an increase in skin cancer.
remediation: The layer of gases around the Earth is the ______.
The lowest layer of the atmosphere is the ______.
In the troposphere, temperature falls by about ______ °C per 1,000 m.
The ozone layer is found in the ______.
Chemicals that destroy the ozone layer are called ______.
The agreement that banned CFCs is the ______ Protocol.
end.homework: Watch or listen to a weather forecast on television or radio. Write down two pieces of information it gives (for example temperature, rain or wind).
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 31: Weather and Climate.
teacherNote: The syllabus asks for an illustration of the main layers only: do not go into details on the mesosphere and thermosphere.
The height of the troposphere varies: about 8 km at the poles and 16–18 km above the Equator (about 12 km on average).
The ozone hole over Antarctica is expected to recover around 2066 (UNEP, 2023).
